entry.title: Charging Animation 1.0.0
entry.content:
Charging Animation

Plays an animation, shows a battery stats card (optionally with sound) when the charger is plugged in or unplugged.

The animation and the card are separate, and either one can be turned off. The settings are split into three groups (BackgroundEffect, Sounds and StatsPanel) plus a single Quiet mode switch at the bottom. Rows that your choices don't use hide themselves, so the list stays short.

Background Effect

When plugged in and When unplugged decide which events play anything at all. The rest of the section is shared by both, apart from the two colors and the unplug direction. The sounds have a section of their own.

There are six looks. Animation picks the one you want.

Wave is the default. It takes a picture of the desktop and bends it outward along an expanding ring, tinted with the event color. Origin moves where it starts, either one of nine spots on the screen under the pointer or Cursor Position to use the pointer itself.

Linear Wave is the same refraction with a straight front instead of a ring. A pair of fronts leave Origin together and run along the line it sits on, one each way, so Top washes the screen downward, Left sweeps it left to right and a corner sends it across at an angle. With Center the two fronts part in the middle and run out to either side. The band of light rides them and Motion shapes the speed in the same way. Reverse on an unplug runs them back in, so the desktop drains toward the origin instead of being pushed away from it.

Edge Glow never touches the desktop. A band of light swells out of the screen borders, and one bright spot travels around them while it's up, coming in from the border nearest Origin. Set the color to rainbow and the band becomes a gradient running around the screen; Motion sets how the spot speeds up and slows down.

Bezel presses the screen in. A dark frame grows out of all four edges, its inner lip catching a little light, and the desktop, captured once when the animation starts, is shrunk to fit inside it, so the whole picture slides inward instead of the edges being covered. Nothing on the picture is stretched: it shrinks by the same amount both ways, so the frame comes out a little thinner across the top and bottom. The picture sinks into the frame's shadow and creeps a little deeper as it settles, then holds and lets go. Because the shrunk picture is a still image, the effect gives up after about two seconds whatever Duration says. While it runs, the monitor keeps showing that still picture, so anything moving on screen looks frozen for those two seconds, even though clicks still reach the windows underneath. The frame is plain black and grey throughout, with no tint on it. Strength sets how far in it comes, about 16 pixels on the long edge at the default. It presses all four edges by the same amount, so it has no starting point and no direction of travel: Origin and Unplug direction are hidden while Bezel is chosen.

Circuit Trace is the quiet one. A circuit board wakes along the bottom of the screen, above the taskbar: a power rail steps across the width of the monitor at forty-five degrees, a bundle of thin signal lines runs beside one stretch of it and fans away at both ends, risers drop off the rail into drilled vias, and elbows turn up out of the bottom corners. A charge runs along each trace in turn, close to white at its head with a long tail of light behind it, and the via it is heading for rings as it arrives. Between pulses the copper only glows faintly, the way a board runs on standby power, and then the whole thing fades out. Nothing is captured from the desktop. Strength sets how thick the traces are and how far their glow spills, and the layout is different on every event. The board runs along the bottom edge rather than around a point, so it has no Origin; Reverse on an unplug sends each charge the other way, out of the far end and back into the rail, so the board drains instead of charging.

Matrix Code is the busy one. Columns of characters drop down the screen, each a bright head over a trail that dims as it falls, and some cells in a trail stay dark, which is what turns a solid bar into a stream of characters. The head of every column keeps flickering to a new character while it travels, and the columns are let go from the Origin outward, so the cascade spreads across the monitor in one sweep. The characters are the event color, with the head of each column close to white, and on rainbow the columns take different points of the gradient. Nothing is captured from the desktop. Strength sets how long the trails are. Like the bezel it is a burst rather than a slow move, so it gives up after about two seconds whatever Duration says. Reverse on an unplug turns the cascade around: the characters run upward, and the release starts at the edges and closes in on Origin instead of spreading out from it.

Colors. Plugged-in color and Unplugged color each tint their own event. Pick one from the list, or choose Custom and type into the field that appears underneath. On Windhawk 2.0 that field is a color picker. These all work:

Format Example
A name purple, mint, gold
Short hex #48F
Hex #4285F4
RGB 66,133,244
Windows accent accent
Rolling gradient rainbow

A name that isn't recognized falls back to the event default, blue for plugging in and red for unplugging, so a typo doesn't break anything.

Strength, Duration, Motion and Opacity control the size and the timing. Strength (0-40) is how far the desktop bends, how wide the light band is, how deep the push goes, how thick the traces are, how long the cascade trails; at 0 the wave keeps only its glow. Duration (300-5000 ms) is how long the animation runs, though the bezel and the cascade stop well before it, Opacity (0-100) fades all of it, and Motion picks the easing used by Wave and Edge Glow.

Dim screen darkens the monitor the animation plays on, the way a phone dims its display when it starts charging. It fades in over the first quarter second, stays down for the length of the animation and fades back out at the end, so nothing snaps. The range is 0-90, so the screen is never fully black. The battery card sits above the dim and stays bright, only the monitor the animation plays on is dimmed, and with the animation turned off for an event there is nothing to dim.

Unplug direction picks which way the unplug travels. Forwards plays it exactly like a plug-in, expanding from the origin; Reverse starts at the screen edges and collapses back to the origin, like the charge being pulled away. Wave, Edge Glow, Circuit Trace and Matrix Code use it, and Bezel hides it because it has nowhere to travel.

Sounds

Both fields take a path to a .wav file, or a system sound alias such as Notification.IM or WindowsBackground. Leave a field empty for no sound. If you want the sound on its own, turn off the animation and the card for that event. If the Charging Sound mod is also set to play on the same event, both sounds will play.

Stats Panel

When plugged in and When unplugged choose which events show the card, so you can keep it for plugging in only, for unplugging only, for both or for neither. The rest of the section applies either way.

Fluent (Windows 11-ish) is the default. It's an acrylic card: the desktop behind it is blurred once when the card appears and covered with the theme color, with a thin border and a soft shadow on top. A battery icon sits in a tinted tile next to the percentage, there's a status line under the number, and a level bar that fills from empty as the card slides in and turns red below 20% while on battery.

Fluent (Minimal) is the same card at badge size, with half the padding, a smaller number, no status line and a thinner bar.

PineApple (Card) is the plain system HUD: a rounded square, as wide as it is tall, black in dark mode and white in light mode, with a large battery icon on top, the percentage below it, the status line under that and a full-width capsule bar along the bottom. The accent color isn't used anywhere in it, and the icon and the bar turn red when the battery runs low. It fades and pops in quickly instead of sliding; Center is the usual place to put it.

Galaxy UI is the wide soft card with corners that take about a third of its height. The percentage is twice the normal size, with a bolt in a round tinted badge next to it, the status line underneath and one thin bar running the full width along the bottom edge. On an unplug the badge shows a battery instead of the bolt. The surface is nearly opaque, so the desktop behind only tints it.

PineApple (Circle) is the phone charging screen: a thick ring that fills clockwise to the battery level, a bolt and the percentage in the middle, and the status line on a small frosted pill underneath. The middle of the dial is a soft patch of the blurred desktop, so the number sits on a little frost instead of bare wallpaper, and the patch fades away before it reaches the ring, which keeps the dial floating instead of turning it into a card. The number and the bolt also carry a soft shadow that keeps them readable on a bright background. It springs in with a small overshoot, sweeps the ring once, and shrinks away when it closes.

The Fluent and Galaxy cards follow the Windows app theme; the PineApple card flips between black and white with it, so it stays readable on either wallpaper. All five update once a second and fade out at the end.

Position, accent and the rest. Position is where the card appears: Follow Effect Origin keeps it where the animation started, and the other choices are the corners, the edges, Center and the cursor. It always stays inside the working area, so the taskbar isn't covered. Accent color sets the tint, with Match Effect Color taking the color from the event that brought the card up (the gradient included) and Custom reading the field below it in any of the formats above; the PineApple card has no tint to give it, so it ignores this one. Turning Details off drops the status line, and Duration, Opacity and Font size tune the rest.

Quiet Mode

While a full-screen app, a game or presentation mode is running, Quiet mode skips the animation, the sound and the card. On a locked screen or during the screen saver there is nobody to see the visuals, so the animation and the card are skipped then as well, whether Quiet mode is on or off, and only the sound plays.

Credits

Wave Effect inspired by Magic Pointer Mod

Power notification handling adapted from Charging Sound

entry.title: GPU-accelerated explorer.exe list and grid views 1.0.4
entry.content:
• Added full touchscreen support, including scrolling, pinch-to-zoom, gestures, and drag-and-drop.
  • Added mouse and touch shortcuts: double-click empty space to go up a folder, middle-click folders to open new tabs, and two-finger tap to open context menus.
  • Improved file tooltips with detailed metadata, including file sizes, dates, dimensions, and localized relative dates.
  • Added selection checkboxes, including a Select All checkbox.
  • Redesigned drag-and-drop previews with stacked icons, thumbnails, and smooth animations.
  • Added support for native Windows 11 context menus.
  • Added persistent folder sorting, synchronized with Explorer's native view.
  • Fixed blurry interface elements and inconsistent DPI scaling.
  • Fixed cloud, network, and virtual folders incorrectly appearing empty.
  • Fixed folders occasionally failing to open or losing selections.
  • Fixed Select All occasionally clearing the selection instead.
  • Fixed missing icons and incorrect shortcut or cloud status overlays.
  • Fixed flickering during window resizing, file renaming, and folder navigation.
  • Fixed Explorer's native view not restoring correctly when switching views.

entry.title: Window Centralizer 1.0.0
entry.content:
Window Centralizer

New dialogs and small windows open centered to where they came from, the mouse cursor, or the monitor, instead of randomly around the screen.

The window is placed before it appears, so there is no jump, no flicker, and window opening animations play at the final position. Elevated programs are covered as well.

Modes

  • Parent window / monitor: centered on the window it came from, otherwise the active or topmost window of the same program. Orphan windows, such as the Run dialog or a program just launched, open centered on the monitor where the mouse cursor is.
  • Parent monitor only: centered on the monitor of the window it came from, or on the monitor with the mouse cursor when orphan. With the window size limit to target at 100%, every window opens at the center of the screen.
  • Mouse cursor: centered on the mouse cursor.

In every mode the window is kept inside the monitor's work area.

Which windows are moved

  • Only windows with a title bar that are smaller than the window size limit to target setting (a percentage of the monitor's work area). Large main windows keep their assigned position.
  • Standard Windows dialogs (Save As, Run, properties pages…) are always centered, whatever their size.
  • Windows of UWP apps such as Calculator and Clock are centered the first time they get focus, so they can be seen jumping after appearing.
  • Maximized, minimized, tool, layered and untitled windows, splash screens, menus, tooltips and shell surfaces (taskbar, Start, search) are never moved. Windows that an animation mod fades in are still centered.
  • A window that is hidden and shown again (for example a Find dialog that is reopened) is centered again.
  • Some programs move their window again right after showing it (Firefox). The mod takes care of that. Initial moves by other tools (FancyZones), and the user's own dragging, are left alone.

Ignoring windows

Press Win+Alt+I while a window is active to stop centering that kind of window. Press it again to undo. A short notification confirms the option.

It covers the kind of window, not the document or page it shows: ignoring one Chrome window ignores every Chrome window, and ignoring the Properties of a folder ignores Properties for every folder. Standard dialogs, which all share one window class, are told apart by the kinds of controls they contain, so Find and Save As stay separate. Dialogs of the same program built from the same kinds of controls, such as simple message boxes, are treated as one kind. UWP apps are told apart by the app's own program, so each one can be ignored separately.

The Ignored windows list opens with Win+Ctrl+Alt+I, and entries can be reviewed and removed there. If its hotkey is empty or taken by another program, that window opens whenever the mod settings are saved.

Both hotkeys can be changed in the mod settings. They run in a small background process started by Windhawk.

Compatibility

Don't use this mod together with Center New Windows. Both reposition windows as they are shown, so the same window would be moved twice, especially dialogs when that mod's "Always center dialogs" option is on.

entry.title: WinTips OSD 1.4.1
entry.content:
• New "Language" setting: follow Windows (simplified Chinese on a Chinese Windows, English on every other language), or pin the card to English or Chinese.
  • Setting names, descriptions and the drop-down option labels are now fully bilingual, so a Chinese Windhawk no longer shows English options next to Chinese labels.
  • Follow an auto-hidden taskbar: the card lifts as the bar slides out and settles back to the screen edge as it retracts, instead of being pinned to the work area.
  • New "Card size" setting (60–200%) that scales the text, icon, accent bar and the ×N badge together.
  • "Show on" now defaults to the display with the active window; "Cursor" and "Primary" are still available.
  • The follow loop caches the taskbar window and monitor handle instead of walking top-level windows 17 times a second.
  • Per-monitor DPI is now read with GetDpiForMonitor, and the taskbar cache is dropped on display or DPI changes.

entry.title: Compiz Desktop Cube for Windows 11 5.9.0
entry.content:
Compiz Desktop Cube for Windows 11

A Compiz / GNOME style 3D desktop prism for Windows 11 virtual desktops. Built on Windows.UI.Composition + Direct2D with a GPU blurred background.

How to use

  1. Press and hold the left mouse button on empty space of the taskbar (works with an auto-hide taskbar too).
  2. Drag upward. The desktop shrinks gradually into the cube.
  3. Keep holding and drag left / right to turn it. After a moment up / down tilts it.
  4. Mouse wheel zooms the cube in and out (scroll up = closer, scroll down = farther). (Optional: set "Mouse Wheel Action" to the window switcher to get the Alt+Tab style window cycling instead.)
  5. Add / remove desktops: while the cube is open, right-click the right edge of the screen to add a desktop (+1) or right-click the left edge to remove one (-1). The frosted gray zones are hidden by default: move the pointer to the far left or far right edge and the matching zone (a - or a +) slides in. It stays while the pointer is inside it, flashes when you use it and hides again. "-" closes the LAST desktop (its windows move to the previous one). The cube rebuilds itself with a little spin and the new face fades in.
  6. Release. The cube snaps to the nearest face and switches desktop. A quick flick also switches. Press Escape to cancel.

Faces follow your desktop count

  • 1 desktop: a single face with limited rotation.
  • 2 desktops: two faces (a flip card).
  • 3, 4, 5, 6 desktops: triangle, cube, pentagon, hexagon.
  • More than 6 desktops: hexagon, faces are re-mapped while you turn it, so every desktop is reachable.

Live desktop

  • The desktop you are on is streamed LIVE (Desktop Duplication) into the front face and into the blurred background. A video that is playing keeps playing, blurred behind the cube and sharp on the face while it turns.
  • The cube overlay is excluded from capture, so it never shows up inside itself.
  • Desktops you are not on are rebuilt from your wallpaper plus a capture of each of their windows (PrintWindow). Windows that cannot be captured are simply left out (no more black placeholder cards). Those faces cannot be live, Windows does not render apps of other virtual desktops.
  • If Desktop Duplication is not available (some hybrid GPU laptops), a slower GDI live capture is used automatically.

Smoothness

  • Persistent render thread, devices stay warm between gestures (pre-warmed as soon as you press the taskbar).
  • Mouse input is read on the render thread, not on the busy taskbar thread.
  • Rendering is locked to the monitor's vertical blank, so it follows 60 / 120 / 144 / 240 Hz by itself. All motion is time based.
  • Live frames are presented without ever blocking the render thread, so a busy GPU can no longer make the cube miss a refresh.
  • Power: no permanent 1 ms timer, normal-ish thread priorities, the blurred background refreshes at a low rate, and while the cube is held still the render loop drops to about 30 Hz (it jumps back to full refresh the instant you move the mouse).
  • Turn on "Enable Diagnostic Logging" to see the measured fps and the monitor Hz in the Windhawk log.

Notes

  • The real taskbar is hidden from the capture, so every face is the full, uncropped desktop (wallpaper where the taskbar was). The taskbar is restored the moment the gesture ends. If Windows refuses to hide it, the old crop is used as a fallback.
  • Window switcher: every window becomes a live thumbnail card (the selected one is refreshed every frame, the others a few times per second). It shows what is visible on screen, so a part hidden behind another window shows that other window.
  • The GPU device is created on the graphics adapter that drives your monitor, so screen capture stays on the fast path.
  • PrintWindow cannot render every app (some games, protected content). Those windows are left out of other desktops' faces.
  • The overlay is hidden from screenshots and screen recorders on purpose (needed for the live capture).
  • Desktop switching sends Win+Ctrl+Left/Right. No undocumented COM is used.
  • Screen recording: turn on "Screen Recording Mode" in the mod settings to make the cube visible to recorders (it applies the next time you open the cube). The front face is a still picture while it is on.
  • The Windows desktop slide animation is hidden only while the cube switches desktops (explorer is told "animations off" for that moment). Your Windows "Animation effects" setting is never changed.
  • If you still see a slide on your build, raise "Switch Settle Delay".

entry.title: Large Icons View for File Explorer 2.0.0
entry.content:
Large Icons View for File Explorer

Keeps File Explorer folders in Large icons view. The icon size is configurable: 96 pixels matches Windows' own Large icons.

How it works

The view is switched when a folder opens in a File Explorer window, without waiting or polling.

  • Keep enforcing (default): if you switch a folder to another view, it is switched back to large icons.
  • With Keep enforcing off, every folder opens in large icons, but a view you pick manually stays until you navigate to another folder.

It applies to file-system folders (local, removable and network drives). The desktop, Open/Save dialogs, Home, This PC, the Recycle Bin and other virtual folders are not affected. Folder contents are never read, moved or changed.

Disabling the mod and restoring views

When Remember each folder's view settings is on (the Windows default), Explorer saves the view of each folder you open. Every folder opened while the mod is enabled is therefore saved in large icons, and keeps that view after the mod is disabled or removed.

To restore the default view of all folders, open Folder Options > View and select Reset Folders.

Credits and links

Original project by Dev_Maycon, developed with AI assistance. Licensed under GPL-3.0-only.

  • Repository: MayconDIS/Windhawk_Mods.
  • GitHub profile: MayconDIS.

entry.title: Taskbar Media Widget 0.3.5
entry.content:
Taskbar Media Widget

A compact media widget for the Windows 10 and Windows 11 taskbar. It reads metadata and controls playback through Global System Media Transport Controls. The media API requires Windows 10 version 1809 or newer, including Windows 11.

On Windows 11, the widget is inserted into the native tray XAML layout and tracks the taskbar height automatically. On the classic 64-bit Windows 10 taskbar, including ExplorerPatcher configurations, it uses a DPI-aware Win32 child window because that taskbar has no XAML tree. It reserves space beside the native task buttons and restores that space when hidden or unloaded.

Widgets are created on the primary and secondary taskbars enabled in Windows. Each taskbar has independent layout and UI state; media polling and audio capture remain shared. On Windows 11 an unavailable XAML host is retried rather than replaced by a floating desktop overlay.

The Taskbar monitors setting selects all monitors, the primary monitor, or one display device. For Selected monitor, the display number identifies the Windows device name (for example, 2 selects \\.\DISPLAY2), not the enumeration order. If that display is disconnected or has no taskbar, the widget stays hidden. Windows can renumber display devices after a connection or driver change.

The native Windows 11 bottom, top, left and right taskbar positions are supported. Left and right taskbars use a compact vertical player that keeps the artwork, playback time, transport controls and progress inside the bar.

Screenshots

Features:

  • album art, title and artist
  • always-visible previous / play-pause / next controls
  • always-visible playback time
  • seekable progress bar with a moving time tooltip
  • title / artist marquee when text overflows
  • artwork-derived progress and visualizer colors
  • a real WASAPI loopback visualizer across the widget background
  • mouse wheel app-volume control with a system-volume fallback
  • compact idle launchers for configured music apps that skip pinned apps
  • automatic layout updates when the taskbar edge or thickness changes
  • per-monitor taskbar instances and DPI-aware classic layouts

Taskbar Fluent Media Player and Island Media Controls already provide rich Windows 11 playback widgets, including audio visualization. This mod focuses on a different compatibility and layout scope: the same UI also supports the 64-bit Windows 10/classic taskbar, native top/left/right taskbar positions, and an idle state that becomes a compact launcher for unpinned music apps. Those features require a second Win32 rendering backend and a distinct launcher state rather than a small option in either Windows 11-only layout.

entry.title: Compact Notifications 1.0
entry.content:
Compact Notifications

Replaces Windows toast banners with compact chat-style cards: black (or white) rounded cards with a round avatar, the sender in bold and up to a few lines of text, sliding in from the screen edge.

What works

  • Click a card to do what clicking the original notification does (open the app or the conversation).
  • × (on hover) closes the card; the notification stays in the notification center.
  • Buttons from the notification (for example Reply, Snooze, Dismiss) are shown under the text.
  • Reply box: click it and type, then press the app's send button. The text goes to the original reply box, so the app receives it as usual.
  • Avatars: the notification's image (local files and images from Store apps), or a thumbnail of its large picture (e.g. a screenshot); otherwise the app's registered icon (e.g. Firefox), and the first letter of the app as the last resort. Web images aren't downloaded.
  • Priority notifications (reminders, alarms, incoming calls) get a colored outline and stay until handled.

Settings

  • Appearance: theme, size, lines of text, card width, corner radius, background opacity, your own card and text colors, distance from the screen edge.
  • Avatars: on or off, circle, rounded square or square, the app's name before the sender.
  • Animation: on or off, speed, how many cards show at once.
  • Position: monitor and corner.
  • Per-app rules: for a single app (by the name shown on its notifications), hide the buttons, the reply box or the avatar, or don't show cards for it at all; its notifications still go to the notification center.

How long a card stays

A card stays exactly as long as the original notification would. Windows sets this time in Settings > Accessibility > Visual effects > Dismiss notifications after this amount of time.

How it works

Windows still creates its own banner, but the mod moves it off the screen and reads it (UI Automation and the notification database). Clicks and typing on a card go to the hidden banner, so every app action works as before. Turning the mod off brings the original banners back.

Limitations

  • Text styles, progress bars and large (hero) images are not shown.
  • While a full-screen app or Do not disturb is on, Windows doesn't show notifications at all, so there are no cards either.
  • The reply box on a card shows the typed text with the caret at the end; moving the caret with the arrow keys or selecting text works, but isn't shown on the card.

entry.title: Modern Run Dialog UI For Windows 10 & 11 4.0.101

entry.title: Taskbar System Utilities 1.0
entry.content:
Taskbar System Utilities

System utilities integrated into the Windows 11 Taskbar XAML context menu with native XAML flyout cards, synchronous UI thread safety, and zero UAC prompts.

Features

  • Restart Explorer: Instantly restarts the explorer.exe shell process from the taskbar context menu.
  • Clean Temp: Comprehensive temporary file cleaner for %TEMP% and accessible files in %WINDIR%\Temp. Deletes all unlocked temporary files regardless of age (relying on Windows file sharing locks to protect actively opened files) and displays a XAML summary card.
  • Clean DNS Cache: Flushes the Windows DNS resolver cache via dnsapi.dll!DnsFlushResolverCache.
  • Restart Graphics Driver: Triggers the Win + Ctrl + Shift + B display driver reset shortcut.
  • Get Local IP: Lists active local IPv4 and IPv6 addresses across network adapters using GetAdaptersAddresses (iphlpapi.dll) with optional clipboard copy.

Credits & Licensing

Taskbar context menu injection hooks adapted from taskbar-restart-explorer by Mgrmjp. This project is distributed under the MIT license.

entry.title: Taskbar Zones 1.0.0
entry.content:
Taskbar Zones

Keep your apps on the left or right side of the Windows 11 taskbar. Each app stays on the side you choose, even when you open or close it.

Features

  • Two fixed zones: Choose the left or right side for each app.
  • Easy drag and drop: Move apps between zones or change their order.
  • Saved layout: Keep your app positions after restarting Explorer or your PC.
  • Custom layout: Adjust spacing and the size of icons on the right.
  • Multiple monitors: Supports compatible secondary taskbars.

How to use

  1. Set your Windows 11 taskbar alignment to Left.
  2. Drag an app icon across the middle gap to move it to the other side.
  3. Drag icons within the same zone to reorder them.
  4. Open the mod settings to adjust the layout.

Notes

  • Your Windows pinned apps are not changed.
  • Do not enable Taskbar Split or other mods that reposition the same icons at the same time.
  • If the taskbar is too crowded to fit both zones, Windows' normal layout is used until space is available again.
  • Secondary monitors show only the app buttons that Windows puts on each taskbar.
  • Windows updates may affect compatibility.

Credits

Taskbar Zones is maintained by Luiz Bizzio. It is a separate, modified version of Taskbar Split by Arkadiusz (Artllex), with persistent per-app zones, cross-zone dragging and secondary taskbar support.

Licensed under GPL-3.0. Additional code credits and copyright notices are in the source file.

entry.title: Taskbar Live HUD 1.0
entry.content:
Taskbar Live HUD

A compact system monitoring widget for the Windows 11 taskbar. Displays real-time CPU usage, RAM load, network traffic, and optional latency, with an optional process memory trimmer.

This is a tool mod: it runs in its own dedicated process instead of being injected into explorer.exe, so it cannot affect the shell's stability and survives Explorer restarts.

Features

  • Real-time monitoring: CPU load, RAM usage and active network speed.
  • Windows 11 look: blends with the taskbar, configurable corner style.
  • Auto-hide: hides itself when a fullscreen game or application is active.
  • Ping (opt-in, off by default): when enabled, an ICMP echo request is sent to the selected public DNS resolver (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1, Google 8.8.8.8 or Quad9 9.9.9.9) roughly every 1.6 seconds. Nothing is sent while it is disabled.
  • Process Memory Trimmer (opt-in, off by default): trims the working sets of all user processes that can be opened with the current privileges. Trimmed pages move to the standby list and programs page the data back in when they need it, so this does not free memory in a lasting way and may cause a short slowdown.

Controls

  • Ctrl + Left Click: trim memory (only if enabled in settings).
  • Alt + Left Click and drag: adjust the horizontal position on the taskbar.

Known limitations

  • Only the primary taskbar is supported (no secondary monitors).
  • Network speed is the sum of all active non-loopback adapters.

entry.title: Win Duo Bar 1.1.4
entry.content:
Win Duo Bar

A compact, minimal ring widget that replaces the Windows 11 notification-area clock. It shows the device status at a glance:

  • Battery ring - a 263 degree gauge with round caps and a translucent track. The filled part follows the battery level; the ring is green while plugged in, red when the battery is low (20% or less), yellow in battery saver mode and uses the taskbar text colour otherwise.
  • Wi-Fi symbol in the middle - two thick rounded arcs plus a solid dot, traced from the original 09 Wi-Fi icon. It switches to the wired/VPN icon when the active connection is not wireless and dims when offline.
  • Time and date - two rows of four bold digits (1427 = 14:27, 1102 = November 2nd), no separators.
  • Charging animation - a notch opens at the top of the ring, a white bolt grows out of it, the Wi-Fi symbol slides down a little and the colours cross-fade (about 0.5 s, 60 fps).
  • One widget per taskbar - every taskbar clock gets its own widget, so multi-monitor setups keep a clock on every taskbar.

Every visual parameter (ring diameter/thickness/gauge span/track opacity/notch angle/bolt size, Wi-Fi size/thickness/opening/position, digits size and row positions) can be adjusted in the mod settings. The settings are localized (English and Simplified Chinese).

The widget is 38 DIP by default. The DIP geometry values below are relative to that default size and scale together with the "Widget size" setting.

This mod replaces the clock only. To hide the system battery and network tray icons, which the widget makes redundant, use the Taskbar tray system icon tweaks mod instead.

Only Windows 11 is supported.

中文说明

Win Duo Bar 是一个替换 Windows 11 通知区域时钟的圆环小组件：

  • 电量圆环：263° 圆环，圆头、带半透明轨道；电量部分随电量变化，插电时绿色、 低电量（≤20%）红色、节电模式黄色，其他情况跟随任务栏文字颜色。
  • Wi-Fi 图标：中间两条粗圆头弧线 + 实心圆点（按原版 09 图标描出）；当前连接 不是无线时显示有线/VPN 图标，断网时变暗。
  • 时间日期：下方两行四位数字（1427=14:27、1102=11月2日），无分隔符。
  • 充电动画：充电时顶部张开豁口、白色闪电长出、Wi-Fi 图标下移、颜色渐变， 约 0.5 秒 60fps。
  • 每个任务栏一个小组件：每个任务栏时钟都有独立的小组件，多显示器任务栏 都会显示。

所有视觉参数（圆环外径/粗细/弧度范围/轨道透明度/豁口角度/闪电大小、Wi-Fi 尺寸/ 粗细/开口/位置、数字字号和两行位置）都能在设置里调整，设置项已本地化 （英文/简体中文）。

小组件默认 38 DIP；下面的 DIP 几何参数以该默认尺寸为基准，并随「小组件尺寸」 设置一起缩放。

本模组只替换时钟。如需隐藏系统托盘的电量和网络图标（小组件已替代它们）， 请使用 Taskbar tray system icon tweaks 模组。

仅支持 Windows 11。

Credits / 致谢

The taskbar XAML access code (XamlRoot lookup, symbol hooks, running code on the taskbar thread) is derived from the Windhawk mods by m417z (GPLv3), including the Taskbar tray system icon tweaks mod. The Wi-Fi symbol geometry is traced from a "09"-style Wi-Fi icon reference.

任务栏 XAML 访问代码（XamlRoot 获取、符号挂钩、任务栏线程执行）派生自 m417z 的 Windhawk 模组（GPLv3）。Wi-Fi 图标几何按 09 风格 参考图标描出。

entry.title: Outlook Refined 0.6
entry.content:
Outlook Refined

Restyles the new Outlook for Windows (olk.exe) from inside its own page. The mod adds one script to each Outlook window when the window is created, and the script stops at once unless the page is one of Outlook's own. It opens no ports and brings nothing of its own down from the network: every asset it draws with is in this file. It reads your account addresses from Outlook's own storage, to label the folder tree, and with the agenda, month grid or Other card on it calls Outlook's mail service as described below.

Restart Outlook after enabling the mod or changing a setting.

What it asks Outlook for. The agenda, month grid and Other inbox card read your calendar and inbox through Outlook's own mail service, from inside its page, signed with the session Outlook already holds: the mod keeps the request headers Outlook sets, in memory, and reuses them. Those features refresh every few minutes while they are on, and each is off until you turn it on. Nothing is stored, logged or sent anywhere else, and no credential is written down.

Where your edits are kept. Groups, renames, folds, account order and the pane and card sizes are saved in Windhawk's own storage for this mod, so they leave when the mod does. State an earlier version wrote into Outlook's own local storage is moved across the first time this one runs. Other Outlook windows that are already open pick up a change as soon as you move into them.

Folder pane: Favorites in groups that fold (right-click a group header for its menu, drag a favorite to move it, Shift+right-click it to rename or move it), per-account compose buttons, a resizable pane, account trees under one foldable heading, accounts reordered by dragging.

Agenda: today and the next days from every account's calendar at the bottom of the folder pane, with a join button for online meetings, under a month grid shaded by booked hours. Other inbox: the newest Other conversations below the Focused list.

Calendar: one row per account, compact time zones, start and end times on event tiles, overlapping events cascaded or merged.

Reading pane: To and Cc on one line, a compact blocked-content bar, a readable body width. Ribbon: the group-name row under the buttons goes.

Print: printing a message prints the message, not the whole window: the panes, ribbon and buttons go, panes that scroll are released so nothing is cut off, quoted replies can be lightened or dropped, pictures and tables are kept whole, and anything too wide for the page is scaled down to fit.

Known limits. Most features find Outlook's own elements by English labels ("Focused", "Other", "Navigation pane", "Reading Pane") and read times written as 1:30 PM, so in another display language, or with a 24-hour clock, those parts quietly do nothing. The folder pane, the agenda and the print layout are the parts that depend on this most.

entry.title: ThinkPad Battery Controls 0.9.17
entry.content:
ThinkPad Battery Controls

Right-click the Windows battery icon to set charging limits, apply saved presets, or temporarily charge to full. Uses Windows 11 menus without an extra tray icon.

The manufacturer should have made these everyday controls part of the Windows battery menu. It is a shame they did not. Feedback and compatibility reports are welcome.

Screenshots

Battery menu

Charge thresholds

Quick charging presets

Manage presets

Battery health

Power controls

Calibration confirmation

Setup

Choose a backend in Windhawk Settings:

  • Integrated Lenovo service (default): no utility download. Requires compatible Lenovo Power Manager service and drivers.
  • Lenovo ChargeThreshold.exe: download Lenovo's utility, save it wherever you prefer on a local drive, and enter its full path in Settings. The mod verifies the reviewed executable before running it. It never downloads, installs or elevates anything. Setup and diagnostics includes the download link. Only Lenovo's version 1.0.0.2 build is accepted; a newer Lenovo build needs a mod update. Choose a folder that other accounts cannot change.

The gear beside the charge summary opens diagnostics and a driver link based on this machine's detected model. No serial number is read or sent. Drivers are installed separately.

Charging and presets

Save up to 20 named presets and choose up to five quick favorites. Manage presets is available in Set charge threshold and at the bottom of Apply charging preset. Quick presets apply to both batteries. Set charge threshold can edit each battery separately or link their limits with the integrated backend. Each result is read back.

Charge to full saves the original limits, disables them temporarily, then restores at 100% or after eight hours. Cancel restores immediately. A newer enabled range from Vantage is preserved. The integrated backend restores each battery separately; Lenovo's executable cannot restore different ranges on two batteries. Select the integrated backend for that situation. Present batteries restore independently; recovery for a missing battery is retained.

Charging limits belong to the laptop, not to one Windows account. Signed-in sessions share recovery records and normally coordinate through a machine-wide lock. If the lock cannot be used, charging commands and recovery continue without coordination immediately. If a holder blocks ten consecutive periodic checks (about five minutes), they also continue without coordination. The menu then says (not coordinated). The mod retries the lock and resumes coordination when it acquires it. During fallback, simultaneous changes in different sessions can overwrite one another. This favors restoring charge limits over waiting indefinitely.

Thresholds persist after this mod is disabled or removed. Disabling or updating the mod ends a pending full-charge request early: it tries to restore your limits first. Signing out, restarting, shutting down or an Explorer crash skips that step; the saved request is then restored the next time the mod runs, at 100% or once its eight hours have passed. If restoration fails, or the mod is removed while it cannot run, limits may remain off and charging can continue to 100% until the mod runs again or you set limits in Vantage. Removing the mod also removes its Windhawk recovery data. Restore protection before removal.

If an initiated write is cancelled before completion, or its utility process is terminated while running, further changes and recovery pause to avoid racing a command still running in Lenovo's service. Ordinary launch failures and completed errors do not trigger this warning. The menu header links the paused state to setup. Saved limits are retained. Restart Windows, then use Setup and diagnostics to acknowledge the restart and resume recovery. This applies to both backends; cancelling a client cannot undo a server write.

Advanced controls

Battery health shows supported readings. Power offers the verified three-state USB control. Always-on USB settings persist after disabling or removing the mod. Advanced > Experimental groups calibration and independent two-battery limits. Both have simulated coverage, not complete physical validation. Set charge threshold applies one range to both batteries; separate ranges are available only through Experimental. Calibration requires a separate confirmation and connected power; it saves current limits and blocks charging edits while running. Cancellation also requires confirmation. Removing the mod during calibration loses saved recovery: check its state and charging limits in Vantage. Cooling and airplane controls remain omitted until supported behavior is verified. Calibration is not a battery-health treatment.

Compatibility

Tested on a ThinkPad P14s Gen 6 AMD with one battery. Two-battery behavior has mock coverage only and is experimental until a two-battery hardware test is completed. The executable backend requires English output. Private taskbar symbols can change after Windows updates. The tray icon hook is placed in SystemTray.dll, an older Taskbar.View.dll or ExplorerExtensions.dll, as Taskbar tray system icon tweaks does.

Author/publisher: Bill Bauman. Apache-2.0. Project-name trademark and attribution terms are in the source repository; Lenovo's executable remains separately licensed. No Lenovo or Microsoft endorsement is implied.

entry.title: Round Everything 1.0.0
entry.content:
Round Everything

Turns the taskbar into a frame around the whole screen. The taskbar keeps its rectangular shape, and the other three screen edges get a band of the same color, pushed inwards by a configurable offset. The visible "screen" becomes a rounded rectangle that sits flush against the taskbar, with one configurable corner radius.

Works with the taskbar on any edge (top, bottom, left, right) and on every monitor. A monitor without a taskbar ("Show my taskbar on all displays" off) gets the frame on all four edges.

How it works

The mod runs inside the taskbar's explorer.exe and creates one layered, always-on-top window per monitor covering the area next to the taskbar: three bands of the configured offset with the rounded corners. The taskbar itself, its background painted in the frame color, is the fourth side. The frame shape is drawn with GDI+ (anti-aliased); the inner area is fully transparent and lets the mouse through, while the painted frame is solid to the mouse, like the taskbar. No explorer function is hooked: the taskbar's XAML tree is reached through a few taskbar.dll symbol lookups (no XAML diagnostics, so it coexists with Taskbar Styler).

  • Color – the frame has one color of your choice, and the taskbar's own background (Taskbar.TaskbarBackground) is painted with it at the same opacity, so the taskbar and the frame are one surface. The taskbar's own background is restored when the mod is turned off.
  • Frame and taskbar come and go together. When the mod starts, the frame appears in the same instant as the taskbar's new look. When the taskbar moves, resizes or rebuilds (changing its position, a taskbar mod reloading) its background turns transparent and the frame goes away the instant the taskbar window moves; once everything has settled - taskbar at its new edge and uncloaked, its corners in place, the work area reserved - the taskbar paints its background again and, from inside that same rendering pass, reveals the frame (re-shaped for the new edge), so the two reach the screen in one composition. When the mod is turned off the frame disappears as the taskbar is handed back.
  • The frame stays visible during Aero Peek (hovering a taskbar thumbnail or the show-desktop corner), like the taskbar itself.
  • Task View (Win+Tab) – the frame goes away and the taskbar's background and monitor corners turn transparent while it is open; everything comes back together when it closes.
  • Full-screen apps – the frame hides on a monitor while a full-screen window (game, video, F11 browser) is showing there, and comes back afterwards.
  • Work area – Shrink the work area to the rounded screen (on by default) pushes the work area inwards so maximized and snapped windows stay inside the frame; turned off, the frame is purely visual: it overlaps the edges of maximized windows and lets the mouse through. Shrinking registers one invisible appbar per frame edge (the same mechanism the taskbar uses), so the shell reserves the space itself; the appbars are removed and the work area returns to normal when the option or the mod is turned off. Extra work-area inset shrinks it further, on all four sides, so a strip of wallpaper stays visible between the frame/taskbar and your windows.
  • Monitor corners – the four outer corners of each monitor are rounded too, so the whole screen reads as a rounded panel: the sliver outside a quarter circle is painted in the Monitor corner color (black by default). The two corners away from the taskbar are part of the frame itself; the two on the taskbar are XAML shapes added inside the taskbar (no extra windows, so nothing to fight over z-order with), click-through, removed when the mod is disabled.
  • Taskbar border line – the taskbar draws a 1px line along its inner edge (BackgroundStroke), which shows up as a seam between the taskbar and the frame. The mod sets that line's opacity to 0 and restores it when disabled.
  • Offsets and radii are in pixels at 100% scaling and scaled per monitor (configurable).

Window corners (dwm.exe)

Windows 11 rounds normal windows with a fixed 8 px radius and draws maximized windows square. With Round window corners on, the mod also runs inside dwm.exe and hooks the corner-radius decision (CTopLevelWindow::GetFloatCornerRadiusForCurrentStyle): every window that Windows would round - normal, snapped or maximized - gets the one Window corner radius you set, and maximized windows are rounded too, so they sit in the rounded screen like cards. Windows that opt out of rounding (DONOTROUND) and small-radius surfaces (menus, tooltips) are left alone. Changes apply at once: DWM is asked to re-evaluate every window (no window's own corner preference is touched). Full-screen windows share the maximized path in DWM, so they get rounded corners as well.

This part needs one manual step. Windhawk doesn't inject into dwm.exe by default (it is on Windhawk's list of critical system processes), so the window-corner part does nothing until you add dwm.exe to the Process inclusion list in Windhawk's advanced settings. The frame, the monitor corners and the work area don't depend on it and work right away. udwm.dll symbols are downloaded by Windhawk on first use.

This does the same job as the Rounded corners for maximized and snapped windows option of the Custom Window Corner Radius mod, through the same hook - the mechanism is the one Alexey Lavrinenko contributed there; use one mod or the other for window corners, not both.

Notes

  • Shell flyouts (Start, notification center, Task View, …) live above the frame, so they are never covered.
  • With the work area reserved, the frame is solid to the mouse, like the taskbar: clicks on it (and on the extra work-area inset strip) go nowhere, which keeps the invisible resize borders of maximized windows underneath from being hit. Without it the frame lets the mouse through.
  • With an auto-hide taskbar the frame spans the whole monitor and the taskbar slides in over it.
  • Setting all offsets to 0 and keeping a radius gives you just the rounded screen corners against the taskbar.

Credits

The taskbar-thread helpers (RunFromWindowThreadTimeout, FindCurrentProcessTaskbarWnd) and the taskbar.dll XAML-root lookup are ported from Taskbar multi-row by m417z, licensed under the GNU GPL v3.0. This mod is published under the same license.

entry.title: Desktop Window Cards 1.8.1
entry.content:
• Excluded programs: a blank entry hides the entries after it. Windhawk returns "" both for a blank array entry and past the end of the list, so the break on an empty entry ended the list at the first blank one. Every program listed after it stopped being excluded, with no warning. The loop now reads the bounded range (256 entries, only on start and on reload) and skips blank entries.
  • Excluded programs: normalization. \r/\n are trimmed along with spaces and quotes, / is accepted in full paths (C:/Program Files/...), and duplicate entries are ignored.
  • Worker: no busy loop on init failure. If the frame timer can't be created, handles[0] is null and MsgWaitForMultipleObjectsEx fails immediately, so the loop spins at 100% CPU. The worker now checks the window classes, controller and frame timer before it starts, logs which one failed, and leaves the loop on WAIT_FAILED.
